sentences.text: Platydyptes is an extinct genus of penguin belonging to the class Aves and the parent group Sphenisciformes. Its name refers to the broad and flat shape of the humerus bone.
The largest species, Platydyptes amiesi, was roughly the size of a king penguin but possessed longer flippers.
All three species were described from fossils found in the north Otago to south Canterbury region of New Zealand's South Island.
The genus was described by Marples in 1952.
This penguin lived in New Zealand between 27.3 and 21.7 million years ago. Fossils date from the Late Oligocene to the Early Miocene.
